candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Matthew (fragments), preserved in J.A. Cramer, Catenae Graecorum Patrum in Novum Testamentum, Vol. I: In Evangelia S. Matthaei et S. Marci (Oxford: University Press, 1840). PD. Greek text also in PG 72 cols. 365-474.
candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Matthew (c. 430 AD)

'The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath': Cyril reads this not as Sabbath-abrogation but as Sabbath-fulfillment in the person of Christ who is himself the Rest toward which the Sabbath always pointed. Tewahedo's distinctive dual-Sabbath observance (Saturday Sänbäte-Ayhud + Sunday Sänbäte-Krǝstiyan) traces theologically to this Cyrillian dual-fulfillment.
